answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and stands that color's Player ID card visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set bearing that color on its backs; remove cards targeting colors that are not playing, but keep each player's own Ambush card. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, keeping their values hidden.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Each player chooses a color and stands its Player ID card visibly in front of them”; “Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing. Keep your own Ambush card”; “Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center; keep their values hidden.”

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen face-down card until cards are revealed; once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “There is no individual turn order.” Vote: “You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, reveal all choices simultaneously.”

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is required. The player or players receiving the most votes are Targets, so Red is the sole Target with three votes versus two each for Blue and Green.
answers.evidence: Vote: “The player receiving the most votes is the Target. If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.”

answers.answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because they tie for the most votes. With neither successfully protected by Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either one of the tied Targets satisfies the voting requirement and may survive that requirement.
answers.evidence: Vote: “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets”; “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: every non-Target who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, and Green voted for Red rather than the sole Target, Blue. Green did not Ambush, so the successful-Ambush exception does not apply.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated, subject to the successful Ambush exception below.”

answers.answer: Red's Ambush adds no vote. Yellow's vote gives Red one vote, and Pink's vote gives Yellow one vote, so Red and Yellow tie for the most votes and both are Targets. Red is a Target and successfully Ambushes, so Red survives and may eliminate one player who voted for Red; Yellow is the only such voter, so Red eliminates Yellow. Pink voted for a Target (Yellow), so Pink survives the voting requirement. Among the named players, Red and Pink survive; Yellow is eliminated.
answers.evidence: Vote: “Ambush cards do not count as votes”; “If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets.” Ambush: successful ambusher “survives and chooses one of the players who voted for them to eliminate.” Vote: “With tied Targets, voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.”

answers.answer: No. A successful Ambush eliminates only one of the four players who voted for the ambusher. The ambusher may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: the successful ambusher “chooses one of the players who voted for them to eliminate” and “cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.”

answers.answer: That player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only when its player is a Target; an Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails.
answers.evidence: Ambush: “An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.”

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the surviving players.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure table: “Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.”

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.” Components: “Gold Bars are cards, not points”; a bar is “one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.”

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Final Showdown cards. They may discuss a bargain, then each secretly selects one card; they reveal both choices simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “each takes a set of Final Showdown cards. They may discuss a bargain, then each secretly selects one card. Reveal both simultaneously.”

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. The players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar for this outcome. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: with none surviving, “Nobody collects the four central bars. Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.” Special Rules: final voters “receive no consolation bar for that outcome.”

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Share: “You get 2; opponent gets 2.”

answers.answer: The Share finalist receives zero central bars, and the Steal finalist receives all four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Share versus Steal: “You get 0; opponent gets 4.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar, and the Steal finalist receives three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Steal: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go finalist receives one central bar, and the Share finalist receives three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go versus Share: “You get 1; opponent gets 3.”

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar. The remaining two stay in the center, and if play continues, deal just two new bars for the next round.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “If both choose Grab One & Go, each finalist receives one central bar. Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.”

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: “If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold”; “give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck”; “Leave all four central bars for the next round, and give no new gold to the central pool.”

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players, it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded”; “With 6–9 players, reach at least 25 points”; “With 10–12 players, reach at least 24 points”; “If more than one player has reached the threshold, the highest point total wins.”

answers.answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown; continue until a single player at the table has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including players eliminated during that round: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: “If those totals are tied, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown; continue until a single player at the table has the highest gold point total.” Turn Structure: “If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.”
